name: Precision Weighting
description: Context-dependent weighting of prediction errors by reliability or precision. Attention modulates the gain on sensory signals, reducing weight on unreliable inputs. Explains how attention affects perception as precision modulation rather than gain.
key_references: Feldman, H., & Friston, K. J. (2010). Attention, uncertainty, and free energy. Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, 4, 215.
Kok, P., Brouwer, G. J., van Gerven, M. A., & de Lange, F. P. (2013). Less is more: expectation sharpens representations in the primary visual cortex. Neuron, 75(2), 265-270.
empirical_evidence: Attention increases thalamic relay gain (Sillito et al.). Neural variability decreases when attention is directed to a stimulus. fMRI studies show reduced activity for expected stimuli (repetition suppression). Behavioral studies show attention enhances contrast sensitivity. Mechanism still debated (neuromodulation vs. gain modulation).

parameters.range: 0 to high precision (unreliable to fully trusted)
